"Kaiser Ng has decided to pursue a new venture after more than five years at Binance, with a transition plan implemented over the last half year," Binance Co-Chief Executive Officer Yi He said in a statement.

MAINZ, Germany, Nov 7 : Bayern Munich secured a 2-1 victory over Mainz in the Bundesliga on Saturday but the form of goalkeeper Manuel Neuer will again be in the spotlight after another error almost produced an equaliser for the home side in the first half. Neuer became Bayern’s oldest player at 40 years, 225 days, overtaking Bernd Dreher, but was forced off with a recurrence of a foot injury that had kept him out of recent matches, replaced before halftime by Jonas Urbig, 23.  Neuer was left flailing at a cross that resulted in Mainz’s Lee Jae-Sung putting the ball in the back of the net with Bayern leading 1-0, though the effort was ruled out for offside. Neuer’s mistake against Augsburg last month which resulted in the fastest-ever Bundesliga goal after eight seconds by Robin Fellhauer was the latest in a growing number for the keeper once regarded among the best in the world.

According to Sofascore using Opta data, that error was his fifth that led to a goal in his previous 17 Bundesliga games, or one every 3.4 matches. In 248 appearances before that, he made just 10 such errors, or one every 24.8 games. FOOT INJURY Neuer played twice since that Augsburg fixture, which ended 2-2, missing four games with the foot injury. He returned for this week’s 2-0 Champions League win at Atletico Madrid. Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane could not find the net against Mainz but did provide two assists for Joshua Kimmich and 18-year-old Lennart Karl as Bayern extended their unbeaten away run in the league to 31 games. They maintained their lead at the top of the Bundesliga from Borussia Dortmund with both clubs on 21 points from nine games. Bayern have a superior goal difference. Dortmund were given a scare by promoted Elversberg but won 2-1 thanks to two goals from Felix Nmecha. Third-placed RB Leipzig, who are three points behind the leaders, won 5-2 at home to Augsburg, while Jonathan Burkardt scored a 93rd-minute equaliser for Eintracht Frankfurt as they drew 2-2 at Paderborn in a battle between two midtable sides.

Source: Reuters

FAST

LUSAIL, Qatar, Nov 7 : Ducati's Marc Marquez won a thrilling, red-flagged sprint at the Qatar Grand Prix on Saturday to put a record-equalling eighth premier class title within reach, while rival Jorge Martin finished third, two weeks after breaking his wrist. Fabio di Giannantonio, the 2023 winner, came second in a sprint that was red-flagged when Ducati's Francesco Bagnaia suffered a painful crash on lap one which resulted in a fractured foot. Marquez and Marco Bezzecchi had been battling for the lead earlier in the sprint but a crash ended not only the Aprilia rider's sprint but also his slim hopes of fighting for the MotoGP title. With a lead of 49 points, reigning champion Marquez can now win a record-equalling eighth premier class title if he wins Sunday's race and Martin does not score any points.

"It was a strange sprint race, especially with the red flag. We hope and we wish that Pecco (Bagnaia) is okay because it was a nasty crash," Marquez said. "But apart from that I was super concentrated. I defended the best way possible." SPRINT RED-FLAGGED Aprilia's polesitter Bezzecchi made the perfect start to take the lead ahead of Marquez, but Bagnaia's sprint did not last a full lap when Fermin Aldeguer cut across and made contact with the Ducati's rear tyre. The impact threw Bagnaia into the air before he landed hard and the sprint was red-flagged as the Italian was taken away on a stretcher. On the restart, Marquez had the better start off the line and the Spaniard took the lead from Bezzecchi while Martin methodically made his way up from 11th to fourth by the end of lap two. Bezzecchi tried to pass Marquez on the inside on lap four and as the two made contact, it was the Aprilia rider who came off worse, losing his balance and sliding out of contention. Stewards took no action on the incident, drawing sarcastic applause from Aprilia boss Massimo Rivola in the garage. MARTIN CHALLENGES MARQUEZ Marquez had barely any time to recover from the collision as he suddenly had Martin attacking him and they traded positions, but the Ducati rider maintained his lead. "When I had the impact, even my airbag deployed. For that reason then, Jorge attacked me because it takes some time to return to normal," Marquez added. However, Martin looked to be tiring and dealing with the pain from his wrist injury as he lost ground to Marquez, soon finding himself battling for second with Di Giannantonio, who overtook him at the end of the sprint. "I'm really proud of the work I'm doing. Twelve days ago, I broke my wrist... With all the adrenaline, I was trying to push," said Martin, who had strapped an ice bag on his wrist after the sprint. "For me, it's already a victory and I hope my story can inspire people throughout the world."

Source: Reuters

PARIS, Nov 7 : World number four Ben Shelton shook off a first-set stumble to beat local favourite Luca Van Assche 5-7 6-3 6-4 and go into the Paris Masters final on Saturday, reaching the third ATP 1000 final of his career. US Open finalist Shelton netted twice from the baseline and hit a forehand wide as Van Assche, ranked 47th in the world, took the only break in the first set to go 6-5 up amid roaring support from his hometown crowd, backed by drum beats and chants. But the third seed, who was undone by his 17 unforced errors in the first set, found his rhythm in the second. He dragged the 22-year-old Frenchman into long rallies to force mistakes and broke to go 4-2 up, a lead that secured the set. Shelton looked shaky early in the third set, landing wide twice as Van Assche took a 3-1 lead with a break. But the American turned the tide back in his favour, winning the next four games while Van Assche struggled with double faults and netted forehands.

EDINBURGH, Nov 7 : New Zealand kept up their unbeaten record against Scotland, blowing away their hosts in the second half as they won 43-21 in imperious style in their Nations Championship at Murrayfield on Saturday. There were 10 tries as both sides showed elements of their running game but errors and yellow cards also impacted on the outcome, with Scotland looking rusty and the All Blacks finishing strongly. Veteran back Beauden Barrett scored two tries to bring his test tally to 50 with Wallace Sititi, Ethan de Groot, Peter Lakai, Josh Moorby and Asafo Aumua also crossing the line for the Kiwis and Damian McKenzie kicking four conversions Hooker Ewan Ashman notched a hat-trick of tries for Scotland in the first half, all converted by Finn Russell.

The win keeps New Zealand alongside South Africa, who thumped Italy earlier on Saturday, on 20 points at the top of the Southern Hemisphere standings but defeat for Scotland comes a heavy blow to their hopes of topping the Northern Hemisphere section. "We played our rugby in the first half but we probably left points out there. We were nowhere near accurate enough second-half, and we couldn't stick with them, it's really disappointing," said Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu. The first of seven first-half tries came in the fourth minute as All Blacks’ attacking intent was signalled straight away with a penalty opportunity spurned and a clever decoy from the resultant lineout allowing Sititi to burst over. IMMEDIATE RESPONSE But there was an immediate response from the hosts after Kyle Rowe’s long kick earned them a 50-22 and, from the resultant lineout, Ashman scored. Two tries in four minutes put the All Blacks 10 points clear in the 20th minute with De Groot bursting over after scrumhalf Cam Roigaard took a quick tap penalty and Lakai scored from a lineout maul to make it 17-7. Yellow cards for Lakai and Sititi meant New Zealand were effectively down to 14 men for the rest of the half with Ashman scoring twice more to complete his treble but in between Barrett crossed for his first try. STEPPED UP A GEAR There was a three-point difference at the break with Scotland still holding out  hopes of ending their 121-year winless streak against New Zealand, who have now won 32 of 34 meetings between the sides with two draws. But the All Blacks stepped up a gear to score three more tries in a second half littered with stoppages as Scotland made many errors and had their captain sent to the sin bin. Josh Moorby’s 48th-minute try in the corner was followed two minutes later by Barrett’s second score and substitute Aumua burst through to claim the last of the All Blacks’ 19 unanswered second-half points in the 67th minute. The gulf in class was all too evident after the break with New Zealand looking much more cohesive, having had an eight-match tour of South Africa and two Bledisloe Cup matches against Australia since July when Scotland last played.  "It's pleasing, we had a tough tour in Africa, came back and played some pretty impressive rugby against Australia. We love playing this style of rugby, keeping the ball on the park," said All Blacks' man of the match Quinn Tupaea. (Writing by Mark Gleeson in Cape Town; Editing by Ed Osmond)

Source: Reuters

SAO PAULO, Nov 7 : Red Bull's Max Verstappen set the fastest time in final practice on Saturday for Formula One's Sao Paulo Grand Prix, finishing ahead of newly crowned champion Kimi Antonelli before qualifying later in the day. The four-times champion clocked one minute 11.622 seconds, 0.025 faster than the 20-year-old Mercedes driver who had topped the second practice at Interlagos circuit on Friday. Verstappen is set to start Sunday's race from the back of the grid after collecting a penalty for an engine change, while Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc also face grid drops for taking new internal combustion engines. McLaren's Lando Norris, fastest in FP1, was third quickest on Saturday, 0.131 off the pace, with Mercedes' George Russell fourth. Russell will take a five-place grid penalty, also for an engine change.

The 41-year-old Briton reported "strange" engine vibrations and smoke in the cockpit over the radio before stopping. Aston Martin's Lance Stroll completed only seven laps due to a suspected energy recovery system issue, finishing last. Brazilian Rafael Camara, making his season debut after replacing Esteban Ocon at Haas, finished the session 15th, ahead of his teammate Oliver Bearman. Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto, the other local driver, was 10th fastest. Qualifying takes place later on Saturday, with rain expected but yet to arrive at the atmospheric Brazilian circuit.

LEEDS, England, Nov 7 : Tottenham Hotspur fans raged after Leeds United's Jayden Bogle escaped a red card for a careless challenge on Mathys Tel that injured the French forward on Saturday, but boss Roberto De Zerbi refused to blame his side's 1-0 Premier League defeat on the decision.  Bogle's clumsy challenge just after the half-hour mark prompted a long VAR review. Referee John Brooks ultimately chose not to book the Leeds player but Tel was forced off shortly afterwards by an ankle injury suffered in the clash, and replaced by Dominic Solanke. "I have a big confidence in the referee, nothing changes if he (Brooks) goes to watch the clip or not, I think. There was the VAR and if they didn't take the right decision, I don't know, but we have confidence. We have to keep the eyes on the performance (and) where we can improve," De Zerbi told broadcaster TNT Sports.  "We didn't play like we can. It's a journey for us because we can learn from this game... there was the solution, there was the space, there was the way to attack and to play better and to defend better."

The departure of Tel seemed to rob Spurs of some of their momentum and De Zerbi said his players were off the pace for the remainder of the game.  "I'm sorry for the result but first of all, I'm sorry for the performance in the second half - we didn't play like a top team, we played without the right spirit, the right character, the right physicality in the duels." Leeds manager Daniel Farke was delighted with his side's first league win since September, and said that Bogle's clash with Tel was not intentional.  "It's a very unlucky outcome that Mathys is injured and we wish him all the best and he can recover quickly," Farke said.  "The last thing Jayden Bogle is is a nasty player. He's possibly the softest player in the whole league. I always call him my butterfly, and I can guarantee it was never out of bad intention."

SAO PAULO, Nov 7 : Formula One will continue to race at Sao Paulo's Interlagos circuit until 2035 after announcing a five-year contract extension on Saturday. The existing contract, under an extension agreed in 2023, had been due to run until 2030. Interlagos, officially named the Autodromo Jose Carlos Pace after Brazil's 1975 race winner, first hosted a world championship grand prix in 1973. It is currently the only South American round of the championship.  The atmospheric circuit has witnessed some major milestones in the sport's history, including the late triple champion Ayrton Senna’s emotional home win in 1991, Kimi Raikkonen winning the 2007 title for Ferrari and Lewis Hamilton's first with McLaren in 2008.

"The passion of our Brazilian fans is extraordinary and every time we return to Interlagos we feel their energy in the grandstands and in the city of Sao Paulo." The announcement came as neighbouring Argentina pushes for a return to the calendar, with Buenos Aires' Oscar y Juan Galvez Autodrome undergoing renovations aimed at achieving FIA Grade One status. Buenos Aires Mayor Jorge Macri, who was at Interlagos this weekend, said on social media that he had met Domenicali and presented a proposal for the sport's return to the Argentine capital, which last hosted a race in 1998. "We have mayors from other cities around the world visiting the circuit here but they will not leave with a contract for their cities," Sao Paulo Mayor Ricardo Nunes told reporters. "What they will take home is very nice memories of a great spectacle that we will hold here this week in Sao Paulo." Formula One said the new contract involved "significant investments" by the city to improve the fan experience. Nunes said the race generated a "major economic and financial gain" for Sao Paulo, estimating that this week's event would move around 2.3 billion reais ($417.78 million) through the local economy. He said hotels, restaurants, taxi drivers and ride-hailing services were benefiting from the influx of visitors. The mayor added that tickets had sold out quickly despite organisers increasing capacity by 7,000 seats compared with last year. Brazilian fans have extra reason to celebrate this weekend, with the country having two Formula One drivers on the grid for the first time in a decade. Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto has been joined by Haas rookie Rafael Camara, who replaced Esteban Ocon, while Argentina is represented by Alpine's Franco Colapinto. ($1 = 5.5053 reais)

LONDON, Nov 7 : An own goal by defender Lucy Bronze against Everton on Saturday cost Chelsea top spot in the Women's Super League as they were held to a 1-1 draw at home, allowing Manchester City to leapfrog them following their 5-0 drubbing of West Ham United.  Bronze headed the ball back across the goal to tee up Sandy Baltimore to score from close range in the 28th minute, but five minutes later her attempted clearance rolled into her own net to put the Toffees level.  The visitors held on for a draw as Chelsea dropped points for the first time since the opening day of the season.  Manchester City made the most of that slip-up as Bunny Shaw's superb goal-scoring form continued, the Jamaican striker netting a hat-trick as her side cantered to an easy win over West Ham, with Aoba Fujino and Iman Beney getting the other goals.  After nine games, City top the standings on 25 points, two ahead of Chelsea, with London City Lionesses, who host Birmingham City on Sunday, third on 16 points.

Nov 7 : South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus believes his policy of gradually introducing new players into the Springbok squad is paying dividends after their thumping 66-7 victory over Italy in a Nations Championship clash in Turin on Saturday. The visitors were without several of their experienced names and scored nine tries against an injury-hit Italy as they made an emphatic start to their November fixtures. Erasmus has gambled at times to bring through new players and grow his squad pool ahead of their 2027 Rugby World Cup defence and he is starting to see the fruits of that policy. "I think the biggest thing is that we've been together for eight years now and we've slowly been bringing new people into the system,” Erasmus told reporters.

LONDON, England, Nov 7 : Arsenal banked another three points in the defence of their Premier League title as their trademark persistence once again paid off in a 1-0 home win over stubborn Hull City on Saturday. It was not fluent or convincing but Martin Odegaard's poacher's goal in the 72nd-minute earned Mikel Arteta's side a sixth league win by a single-goal margin this season. Arsenal moved to 27 points from 10 games, six clear of second-placed Manchester City who will try to bounce back from consecutive defeats at Nottingham Forest later on Saturday. Tottenham Hotspur's recent revival came to a halt as they went down 1-0 at Leeds United for whom Noah Okafor struck the winner 97 seconds after coming off the bench at Elland Road.

There was controversy, though, with Leeds fortunate not to be reduced to 10 men in the first half when Jayden Bogle escaped a red card for a dangerous tackle on Mathys Tel. Fulham and Newcastle United shared the spoils in a 1-1 draw at Craven Cottage - Jacob Murphy giving the hosts a late lead only for Rodrigo Muniz to equalise. Arsenal showed last season a champions knack for picking up wins even without hitting top gear and it was very much in evidence against a Hull side who provided a stern test. Captain Odegaard had not scored since September but was on hand to snaffle a rebound after Noni Madueke's shot had been saved by Hull keeper Konstantinos Tzolakis. Tottenham were seeking a fourth successive win but faded against Leeds and Okafor drove home a low shot from the edge of the area in the 79th minute. That proved enough for Leeds to end a five-match winless league run and move above Tottenham into eighth place with 14 points. Tottenham have 12 points. Tottenham fans were furious that Bogle was spared any punishment for his rash lunge on Tel which resulted in the Tottenham winger being forced off with an ankle injury - the VAR check on the challenge taking four minutes. Visiting manager Roberto de Zerbi played down the controversy, however. "I'm sorry for the result, but first of all I'm sorry for the performance in the second half," the Italian said. "We didn't play like a top team, we played without the right spirit, the right character, the right physicality in the duels."

TURIN, Italy, Nov 7 : South Africa strolled past an injury-hit Italy with a 66-7 win in Saturday's Nations Championship meeting in Turin, where flyhalf Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu scored the first of nine Springbok tries and added another 21 points from a perfect kicking display. South Africa ran in six tries in an utterly dominant opening half. Hooker Malcolm Marx went over twice, adding to scores by Feinberg-Mngomezulu, Morne van den Berg, captain Siya Kolisi and Damian Willemse, with Feinberg-Mngomezulu kicking all six conversions having opened the scoring with a penalty. Wilco Louw added another try after the break before Italy finally got off the mark with Federico Ruzza's try converted by Tommaso Allan. Paul de Villiers and Ethan Hooker added to the Springboks' try count. South Africa had claimed maximum points from their three July fixtures to top the Southern Hemisphere group ahead of New Zealand on points difference and they added to that total against Italy ahead of the All Blacks facing Scotland at Murrayfield later on Saturday.

Italy, who lost all three July matches, were without a string of key players, including captain Michele Lamaro and centre pairing Tommaso Menoncello and Juan Ignacio Brex, and had no answer to Rassie Erasmus' almost full-strength side. "They were missing a lot of players and we know very well that things will be different at next year’s World Cup," Erasmus said. "They made the most of their opportunities and caused us problems in the scrum." It was one-way traffic from the off. Italy conceded an early penalty under their posts. South Africa, surprisingly, opted to take the three points, and Feinberg-Mngomezulu followed up with a ninth-minute try. The flyhalf split the Italian defence with a dummy before racing in from 40 metres and the Springboks quickly added two driving lineout tries from Van den Berg and Marx. Feinberg-Mngomezulu sent a booming 50-22 which set up Kolisi's try and in the 25th minute Willemse walked in after Jasper Wiese's pass. Italy spent the final 10 minutes of the half down to 14 men after Muhamed Hasa picked up a yellow card and Marx scored his second try from a maul. SECOND-HALF SLOWDOWN South Africa had inflicted Italy's record defeat with a 101-0 win in 1999 and, at 45-0 down at halftime, the hosts may have feared even worse was in store. The Italians, however, improved somewhat after the break and the Springboks took their foot off the gas a little, although Louw powered over five minutes into the second half for another South African try. Italy lock Ruzza gave the home crowd something to cheer about, going over in the corner but De Villiers went over after another unstoppable maul and Hooker ran in the final score on the stroke of full-time as South Africa earned their biggest win on Italian soil. South Africa are in Paris on Friday to take on France and face Ireland in Dublin eight days later. Italy host Argentina in Genoa next Saturday and Fiji in Udine one week later.

PERTH, Nov 7 : England white-ball coach Brendon McCullum is confident his batsmen will negate any short-ball challenge Australia present in the first one-dayer at Perth Stadium, having acclimatised to conditions with a warm-up game at the WACA Ground on Saturday. England defeated Western Australia by 92 runs in their only hit-out before the three-match one-day international series begins on Friday. "When you come here with the bigger boundaries, the short ball is always a weapon for a bowler. You've still got to find ways to score off it, you can't just keep going under it," McCullum told reporters. "Our boys are all very good players of the short ball."

England had been criticised last year for playing an intra-club practice match at the slow-and-low Lilac Hill, a suburban ground which bore no resemblance to the fast-and-bouncy Perth Stadium where they lost the Ashes opener inside two days. The WACA Ground - now a boutique venue with grassy banks, community pools and gymnasiums - has retained its traditional seam-friendly characteristics though, and paceman Jofra Archer looked particularly menacing for the tourists with 3-34. "He looked like he was charging in nicely... he's got skills at the top, in the middle and at the death so it was nice for him to get through some overs," said McCullum, who has lost seamer Josh Tongue to a left big toe injury. "We love coming out here and playing against Australia. It's always a great contest, albeit their side looks slightly different than it normally does, there's never a weak Australian side." The hosts are resting veteran pace trio Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc. ODI squad member Mahli Beardman went wicketless in the tour match while fellow seamer Lance Morris marked his return from a 20-month back injury with 3-29, at times hitting 145 kph. Opener Ben Duckett top-scored with 59 for England, who were bowled out for 251, but the match highlight belonged to captain Harry Brook who landed a six in the WACA swimming pool. Spinner Adil Rashid took 4-35 as WA collapsed to 159 all out in reply. The ODI series will be followed by five Twenty20 internationals.

Nov 7 : Russian President Vladimir Putin has expanded the list of Japan Tobacco International (JTI) businesses placed under temporary administration in Russia, adding three more companies to those included in the original order issued on Thursday. On Thursday, Putin signed a decree transferring the Russian assets of JTI, part of Japan Tobacco Inc. and Russia's largest tobacco manufacturer, to temporary management, making the tobacco group the latest foreign company to lose control of local operations as Moscow tightens its grip on overseas-owned assets. According to the original decree, the stakes in four JTI businesses were placed under the administration of Russian company Industrial Assets. A separate decree, published overnight, extended the measure to three additional companies, all owned by JTI Investments Sarl According to Interfax news agency, the three firms acted as import, management and holding companies.

Separately, Russian media outlet RBC on Saturday quoted Anton Pivovarov, head of Industrial Assets, as saying the company would seek to maintain production, preserve existing teams and fulfil obligations to employees and business partners without disruption. Putin's decrees gave no reason for the move, but the Kremlin has previously linked similar asset seizures to actions taken by countries it considers hostile to Russia. In an emailed statement issued after the first decree, JTI said it was aware of the decision and was "assessing the situation and our options, prioritising our stakeholders, most notably our employees". The Japanese government owns around 37 per cent of shares in Japan Tobacco Inc., whose brands include Winston and Camel cigarettes. The Russian business accounts for about 10 per cent of Japan Tobacco Group's revenue and roughly 25 per cent of its operating profit.

Source: Reuters
